territorial_scope.description: Applies to assessment mechanisms conducting eye assessments or generating prescriptions in Rhode Island.

evidence.quote: An assessment mechanism to conduct an eye assessment or to generate a prescription for contact lenses or visual aid glasses in Rhode Island shall:

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Adds Rhode Island chapter 97 (Consumer Protection in Eye Care Act) to Title 23. It sets conditions for eye assessments and contact lens or eyeglass prescriptions made through assessment mechanisms, including AI devices, and imposes civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. Takes effect upon passage.
summary.long: Adds chapter 97, the Consumer Protection in Eye Care Act, to Title 23 (Health and Safety). It defines 'assessment mechanism' as automated or virtual equipment, applications or technologies used for eye assessments, expressly including artificial intelligence devices. Assessment mechanisms used to conduct an eye assessment or generate a prescription for contact lenses or visual aid glasses in Rhode Island must provide patient-provider interaction, collect medical history, and disclose as a term of use that the assessment does not replace an in-person examination and has limits on use. Providers using them must be actively licensed, meet in-person standards of care, not rely solely on assessment data for a prescription, verify patient identity and age (18 or older), and confirm recent in-person examinations. Violations carry a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, with administrative hearings and appeal to superior court. The Department of Health must adopt rules. The act takes effect upon passage.

thresholds.value_text: at least eighteen (18) years of age

thresholds.variable_text: time since last in-person comprehensive eye health examination
thresholds.measurement: Look-back window measured from the assessment; the patient's in-person examination must fall within it
thresholds.consequence: An assessment may be used only if the patient had an in-person examination within the window, and only for the stated purposes
thresholds.conditions: Applies to eye assessments and to prescriptions for visual aid glasses; disclosure and advance acceptance as a term of use are also required

thresholds.consequence: Provider may issue a prescription for visual aid glasses only after verifying an in-person examination within the window

evidence.quote: verify that the patient has received an in-person comprehensive eye examination by a provider within the previous twenty-four (24) months

thresholds.variable_text: time from initial prescription or first renewal to in-person comprehensive eye health examination
thresholds.value_text: Within twenty-four (24) months after the follow-up or first renewal of the initial prescription, and every twenty-four (24) months thereafter
thresholds.measurement: Verified by the provider; interval counted from the follow-up or first renewal and repeated thereafter
thresholds.consequence: Provider may issue a contact lens prescription only if an in-person comprehensive eye health examination is verified within the stated intervals

evidence.quote: Within twenty-four (24) months after the follow-up or first renewal of the initial prescription, and every twenty-four (24) months thereafter.
"Assessment mechanism" means automated or virtual equipment, application, or technology designed to be used on a telephone, a computer, or an Internet-accessible device
"Contact lens" means any lens placed directly on the surface of the eye, regardless of whether or not it is intended to correct a visual defect
"Eye assessment" means an assessment of the ocular health and visual status of a patient
"Person" means an individual, corporation, trust, partnership, incorporated or unincorporated association, and any other legal entity.
"Prescription" means a handwritten or electronic order issued by a provider that includes:
"Provider" means a health care professional licensed under chapters 35.1 or 37 of title 5 of the general laws.
"Visual aid glasses" means eyeglasses, spectacles, or lenses designed or used to correct visual defects

obligations.summary: An assessment mechanism used for an eye assessment or to generate a prescription must provide synchronous or asynchronous patient-provider interaction and collect the patient's medical history, previous corrective eyewear prescription, and time since the most recent in-person comprehensive eye health examination. The text does not name the operator of the mechanism.

obligations.summary: Disclose to patients, and require acceptance in advance as a term of use, that the assessment is not a replacement for an in-person comprehensive eye health examination; cannot generate an initial contact lens prescription or a follow-up or first renewal; may be used for visual aid glasses only if the patient had an in-person examination within the previous 24 months; and that CDC advises contact lens wearers to see an eye doctor at least once a year.
